_comment: Tracked, pure-data app configuration. Settings exposed in the dashboard UI (OOR threshold, slippage, intervals, etc.) live in app-config/app-defaults-for-user-configurable/bot-config-defaults.json instead, with per-install operator overrides in app-config/user-configurable/bot-config-defaults.json and per-position runtime overrides in app-config/user-configurable/bot-config.json.

shutdown._comment: How a stop ends the server. On SIGINT or SIGTERM (Ctrl+C, or `npm stop`) the server starts stopping every position and closing its listener, then exits by itself once exitTimeoutMs has passed, finished or not. `npm stop` sends that SIGTERM, then checks every stopCheckIntervalMs whether the server has gone, and only after exitTimeoutMs + stopKillMarginMs falls back to SIGKILL. The margin keeps the server's own exit ahead of the kill, so a stop that is merely slow still runs the steps an exit runs, the PID file's removal among them. Each is checked as a timer setting by src/timer-bounds.js, and an unusable one stops the program reading it, naming the setting, rather than leaving a stop that kills at once. Read by src/shutdown-timing.js, for server.js and scripts/stop.js.

defaults._comment: chain: which entry of chains.json the app runs against when CHAIN_NAME is not set in .env. Read by src/runtime-flags.js, which lowercases it and looks it up in chains.json; a value matching no entry there throws at startup rather than falling back to another chain, since the entry carries the RPC endpoints and contract addresses every transaction is built against. Per feedback_one_literal_per_shipped_default the chain name lives here only.

tx._comment: TX recovery pipeline timing, cross-chain. speedupSec: after this many seconds of the original TX not confirming, submit a same-nonce replacement with 1.5x gas (Phase 2 of _waitOrSpeedUp). deadlineSec: on-chain contract deadline (`require(block.timestamp <= deadline)`) stamped into removeLiquidity / swap / mint calldata. cancelToDeadlineMultiple: the bot's per-TX give-up timer (TX_CANCEL_SEC in code) is derived as deadlineSec × cancelToDeadlineMultiple — how much total time to wait before sending a 0-PLS self-transfer cancel at the stuck nonce. Rule of thumb: set the multiple ≥ 4 so a slow-chain retry cycle can complete before the bot gives up on the nonce. See src/config.js for the derivation and src/rebalancer-pools.js for the deadline enforcement.
tx._cancelPhaseFloorSec_comment: The least time, in seconds, a sped-up transaction gets to confirm before the zero-value cancel goes out. The speed-up's wait normally runs until TX_CANCEL_SEC has passed since the original was sent; when getting the speed-up sent took that long already (its send backs off between retries), the wait still lasts this long, so the replacement is never cancelled the moment it is sent.
tx._sendRetries_comment: How often a transaction whose sending failed for a passing reason (a timeout, a dropped connection, a rate limit) is sent again, and how long to wait first. The wait grows with each try: sendRetryBaseDelayMs before the first retry, twice that before the second, and so on, so the defaults wait 30, 60 and 90 seconds. 0 retries sends once and gives up on the first such failure. A failure that says the transaction can never go through is not retried. Read by src/tx-retry.js for every send in the app. sendRetryBaseDelayMs is checked as a timer setting by src/timer-bounds.js, and both stop startup when unusable, naming the setting.

dashboard._comment: pollsBeforeAssumedSeen: how many of the dashboard's poll intervals (ui-defaults.json → dashboardPollIntervalMs) the server waits, after changing something the dashboard has to show, before it assumes the dashboard has polled and shown it. 2.5 covers two whole polls even when one went out just before the change. The server waits this long before retiring a position whose re-open failed, so the alert about it is on screen first, and the dashboard keeps the Manage button disabled for the same time after a retire. Server-side only: the dashboard receives the resulting milliseconds on GET /api/status as guaranteedDashboardHasPolledMs. At least 1, at most 100; src/config.js stops startup otherwise, naming it.

rescanPrices._comment: How long the dashboard's Re-scan Prices dialog waits for the scan it started before handing the button back, rather than spinning forever. Read by public/dashboard-rescan-prices.js via the rescanPricesTimeoutMs field on GET /api/status. It bounds a button, not a scan: nothing server-side reads it, and the scan it is waiting on runs to completion either way.

compound._repositionWindowSec_comment: Compound detection: an IncreaseLiquidity on an NFT within this many seconds after a DecreaseLiquidity that drained it is a reposition (a drain, then a re-deposit), not a compound, and its amounts are not counted as compounded fees. Turned into blocks with the active chain's blockTimeSec in chains.json, so the window is the same length of time on every chain. 500000 s is about 5.8 days: 50,000 blocks at ten seconds a block.
